title: Donald Knuth and Literate Programming (1984)
explainer: In 1984, Donald Knuth argued that a program's primary audience should be other human beings, not the compiler, and built a system (WEB) for interleaving prose explanation with code so a program could be read more like an essay than a set of instructions. The skill this lesson builds — making sense of someone else's real, unannotated code — is the mirror image of Knuth's complaint: most code you will ever read was never written with a reader in mind, which is exactly why reading it well is a skill rather than a formality.
